candidates.rule: Seller counter and accept offers must not go below 90% of list price; the seller prompt must disclose that floor.
candidates.quote: 71 of 312 seller act calls were refused below the 90%-of-list floor the prompt never showed
candidates.harness: Show the 90% list-price floor in the seller prompt and enforce the same floor in seller actions.

candidates.rule: On the home PC, a seller decision averaged 1.88 model calls versus 1.52 on the laptop, and 27% of decisions took three calls; 71 of 312 seller action calls were refused below the undisclosed floor.
candidates.quote: on the home PC a decision took 1.88 model calls (laptop 1.52; 27% took three) because 71 of 312 seller act calls were refused below the 90%-of-list floor
candidates.harness: Track calls per decision and refusals, and address avoidable refusals by exposing action constraints to the agent.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user said the home PC used the same Claude account as the laptop, making the prompt the lever for reducing calls; the L1 prompt was about 4,000 tokens and should be cut when needed.
candidates.quote: user 11/4: same Claude account as the laptop, so the prompt is the lever; HARNESS 7: L1 prompt about 4,000 tokens, cut it when needed
candidates.harness: Treat prompt improvements, including reducing prompt length when needed, as the lever for reducing model calls.

candidates.rule: The D34 design has the outer analysis set playbook rules, tools execute those rules at once, and the agent handle exceptions; analysts and the strategy agent read recorded exceptions back.
candidates.quote: the seller, buyer and restock run the playbook the outer analysis sets as rules that call the tools at once, and hand only exceptions to the agent; every exception is recorded and read back
candidates.harness: Execute routine playbook actions directly, record exceptions, and make them available to analysts and the strategy agent.

candidates.rule: Before switching to the D34 design, run five steps in shadow mode and wait for the user's review.
candidates.quote: five steps with shadow runs before switching; waiting for the user's review
candidates.harness: Require five shadow-run steps and user review before switching.

candidates.rule: The outer loop must measure latency, calls per decision, refusals, buys per window, and funnels, and alert on health issues.
candidates.quote: the outer loop keeps measuring health (latency, calls per decision, refusals, buys per window, funnels) and alerts
candidates.harness: Measure those health metrics continuously and generate alerts.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user decided restock should buy a list fixed in advance because the rules' numbers keep changing.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 02:1x: the rules' numbers keep changing; restock buys a list fixed in advance
candidates.harness: Use a precomputed restock buy list rather than asking the model to choose routine restock purchases.

candidates.rule: Build the restock list from missed requests, the shop's sales, and the market's best-selling goods; calculate quantities from units per supply window times cover windows.
candidates.quote: restock builds the buy list from our missed requests, our sales and the market's best-selling goods (units per supply window x cover_windows)
candidates.harness: Include those three demand sources and calculate target quantities using units per supply window and cover windows.

candidates.rule: Restock buys each deficient list line at most once per window without the model; the agent runs only when the list produces nothing, as an anomaly.
candidates.quote: buys what each line lacks at once, once per window, without the model; the agent runs only when the list gives nothing (an exec.anomaly event)
candidates.harness: Buy deficient lines once per open window without a model call, and use an anomaly path if the list yields no purchase.

candidates.rule: Default restock coverage is two windows, and the default market-top list contains five goods at two units each.
candidates.quote: playbook.restock numbers default to cover 2 windows, market top 5 x 2 units
candidates.harness: Use two windows of coverage and five market-top goods at two units each as defaults.

candidates.rule: Fit restock lines in list order, taking the most units each line can afford and stock; do not discard earlier lines merely because a later line does not fit.
candidates.quote: act.buy fitting now takes lines in order, each with the most units the cash and stock checks pass
candidates.harness: Allocate affordable, in-stock quantities line by line in list order.

candidates.rule: Restock cash available is balance minus the cash floor and warranty reserve, and available stock room must be checked once before allocating the buy list.
candidates.quote: check.room gives cash (balance - floor - warranty reserve) and stock room once
candidates.harness: Calculate the spend budget and stock room before allocating restock purchases.

candidates.rule: Allocate each buy-list line within the available budget and record that budget; merge lines for the same SKU and preserve the actual refusal reason when a line cannot be filled.
candidates.quote: The buy list allocates each line within it and records the budget
candidates.harness: Enforce and record the budget, merge duplicate-SKU lines, and retain actual refusal reasons.

candidates.rule: Buy only while the market window is open; do not call the agent when the list is full or funds are tied up, and report a no-budget anomaly instead.
candidates.quote: the rules buy only when the window is open ... and never call the agent when the list is full or the money is tied (an exec.anomaly no_budget instead)
candidates.harness: Check the window and available funds before buying; skip the agent call when no purchase is possible and emit a no-budget anomaly.

candidates.rule: The buyer posts only purchase records with their ledger line and does not post wanted items.
candidates.quote: the buyer posts only purchase records with their ledger line (no wanted posts)
candidates.harness: Allow buyer forum posts only for purchases that include the corresponding ledger line.

candidates.rule: Playbook changes merge across two levels; night and delegated installs must preserve the round-end stop and food share.
candidates.quote: playbook changes merge two levels, night/delegated installs keep the round-end stop and the food share
candidates.harness: Merge playbook changes across both levels and preserve the round-end stop and food-share setting in night and delegated installs.

candidates.rule: Do not install a brief written on an older version unless installation is explicitly allowed with --stale-ok.
candidates.quote: a brief written on an older version is not installed without --stale-ok
candidates.harness: Reject stale briefs unless the operator explicitly permits installation with stale-ok.

candidates.rule: Night and delegated installs must not set prices below 80% of list price.
candidates.quote: night/delegated installs also hold a price floor below 80% of list
candidates.harness: Enforce the 80%-of-list floor for night and delegated installs.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user decided to put more idle cash into stock.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 02:2x: the cash sits idle, put more into stock
candidates.harness: Apply the user's revised cash and stock settings rather than leaving the prior allocation unchanged.

candidates.rule: Strategy v18 set the warranty reserve to 10% of sales in warranty, the cash floor to 1,000,000 with a 500,000 bankruptcy line, and the stock cap to 60%.
candidates.quote: warranty reserve 50% -> 10% of sales in warranty (market broke 21 of 4,057 settles, ours 0), cash floor 1.5M -> 1.0M (bankruptcy line 0.5M), stock cap 45% -> 60%
candidates.harness: Use the stated reserve, cash floor, bankruptcy line, and stock cap when calculating available restock funds and stock limits.

candidates.rule: After the v18 changes, cash available for restock rose from 154,924 to 2,326,012, and the next window's buy list planned 928,727; the stock cap then bound.
candidates.quote: cash restock may spend went from 154,924 to 2,326,012 and the next window's list plans 928,727 (now the stock cap binds)
candidates.harness: Monitor restock spending and whether the cash budget or stock cap is the binding constraint.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user's priority was to recover the early loss by selling many units at a profit, judging changes by settled deals and profit per deal.
candidates.quote: the user's goal first in the priorities (11/4 02:2x: win back the early loss by selling many units at a profit; judge changes by deals settled and profit per deal)
candidates.harness: Prioritize profitable unit sales and evaluate strategy changes using settled deals and profit per deal.

candidates.rule: The user can ask the strategy agent to judge a choice such as restock breadth versus depth, and user notes must inform its brief.
candidates.quote: the user can ask the strategy agent to judge now (11/4 02:2x: breadth or depth for restock)
candidates.harness: Include user notes when presenting strategy questions to the strategy agent.

candidates.rule: A restock line's share of the window's money can be capped, and the market-top list can contain up to 30 goods.
candidates.quote: playbook.restock.max_line_share caps one line's share of the window's money and market_top goes up to 30
candidates.harness: Support a maximum share per restock line and market-top lists of up to 30 goods.

candidates.rule: The buyer's first food message must state the required shelf life; shops may refuse food orders when that requirement is omitted.
candidates.quote: the buyer's first message no longer states the shelf life it needs - after 01:47 food orders reached agreement 2 of 26 times (14 shops refused at the first message)
candidates.harness: State the required shelf life in the buyer's first food-order message.

candidates.rule: After 01:47, food orders reached agreement 2 times out of 26; before that, they reached agreement 44 times out of 118.
candidates.quote: after 01:47 food orders reached agreement 2 of 26 times ... before it 44 of 118
candidates.harness: Track food-order agreement rates and flag regressions after buyer-message changes.

candidates.rule: Food that spoils is worth zero, and the kit refuses to pay for food unless its shelf-life hours are provided.
candidates.quote: the kit still refuses to pay food without the hours (food that spoils is worth 0)
candidates.harness: Require shelf-life hours before paying for food, and treat food that spoils as having zero value.
